This guide walks through using Apollo's pre-configured template to create a Dynatrace dashboard and monitor your Apollo Router.

The dashboard is organized to follow a typical investigation workflow, from high-level health to specific subsystems:

- **Overview**: request rate, 5xx errors, p95 latency, in-flight requests, SLA compliance
- **Traffic**: requests by status code, operations by type, request and response body sizes
- **Latency and overhead**: router latency percentiles, router overhead vs subgraph time, per-subgraph latency
- **Errors**: GraphQL errors by code, subgraph errors by subgraph, 5xx over time
- **Saturation**: open connections, compute job queue depth and duration
- **Cache and query planning**: cache hit rates, query planning latency
- **Connector HTTP** and **Coprocessors**: populated only when those features are in use
- **Traces and dependencies**: top operations by p99, failed request exemplars, dependency volumes, error logs

Some tiles are empty by design and say so in their titles: cache tiles require router caching, connector tiles require Apollo Connectors, and the error log tile requires forwarding the router's stdout (the router has no OTLP log exporter).

## Prerequisites

- Metrics and traces exporters configured per the [metrics](/graphos/routing/observability/router-telemetry-otel/apm-guides/dynatrace/dynatrace-metrics) and [traces](/graphos/routing/observability/router-telemetry-otel/apm-guides/dynatrace/dynatrace-traces) guides
- The instruments configuration shipped alongside the template (`instruments.router.yaml`), which enables the standard and custom instruments the tiles query
- Span error marking, so failed GraphQL requests appear as failures:

<Note>

The exporter configuration on the metrics and traces guides is deliberately minimal — it gets data flowing, but on its own it enables none of the custom counters (`dynatrace.router.requests`, `apollo.router.overhead`, `subgraph.name` attribution) this dashboard charts. Deploying exporters without instruments is the most common reason an imported dashboard looks mostly empty. Use `complete-configuration.router.yaml` from the template directory (below) to deploy exporters, instruments, and spans together in one block.

</Note>

```yaml title="router.yaml"
telemetry:
  instrumentation:
    spans:
      mode: spec_compliant
      supergraph:
        attributes:
          otel.status_code:
            static: ERROR
            condition:
              eq:
                - true
                - on_graphql_error: true
          error.message:
            response_errors: $[0].message
```

<Note>

GraphQL errors are returned with HTTP 200. Without the `otel.status_code` attribute above, Dynatrace sees every request as successful and the dashboard's failure rate stays flat while clients receive errors.

</Note>

## Get the template

The template lives in the [`dynatrace/` directory of the apm-templates repository](https://github.com/apollographql/apm-templates). It contains the dashboard JSON, an import script, `complete-configuration.router.yaml` (exporters + instruments + spans in one paste-ready block — start here), the same configuration split into separate files for review, and a DQL query reference.

## Set your service name

Every tile filters on `service.name`, with a default of `apollo-router`. If your router reports a different service name, the import succeeds but every tile is empty. Dynatrace Platform dashboards don't support template variables, so re-target the JSON before importing. The string `apollo-router` appears only inside that filter, so a find-and-replace is safe and complete:

```bash
sed -i 's/apollo-router/my-supergraph/g' dashboard-template.json
```

## Import the dashboard

Import the dashboard JSON using either method:

1. **Platform Documents API**: `POST` the JSON to `https://{env-id}.apps.dynatrace.com/platform/document/v1/documents` with a platform token that has the `document:documents:write` scope, or use the import script in the template directory.
2. **Manual upload**: In the Dynatrace **Dashboards** app, select **Upload** and choose the JSON file.

<Caution>

The Documents API requires a **platform token** sent as `Authorization: Bearer dt0s16...`—not the `Api-Token` access token used for OTLP ingest. Using the ingest token returns a 401 that's easy to misread as an ingest problem.

</Caution>

## Interpret the dashboard

- **Latency percentiles come from spans, not the duration histogram.** DQL's `percentile()` over a rolled-up metric returns the average, so p50, p95, and p99 on the histogram would all show the same number. The template's percentile tiles query `fetch spans` instead, and are subject to your trace sampling rate.
- **Counters arrive with delta temporality**, so `sum()` over an interval is the count for that interval—no rate or diff function is needed.
- **Some duration histograms appear in Grail with a `.seconds` suffix** appended to the instrument name. If a metric tile shows no data, search Grail for both spellings.

## Troubleshoot

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| Every tile is empty | `service.name` doesn't match the dashboard filter; re-target the JSON and re-import |
| Most tiles are empty, but a few (like in-flight requests) show data | Only the exporter config was deployed, not the instruments/spans blocks — deploy `complete-configuration.router.yaml` in full, not just the exporters |
| Only the cache, connector, coprocessor, or log tiles are empty | Expected — those tiles require a router feature (entity caching, Apollo Connectors, a coprocessor, or log forwarding) that most graphs don't enable |
| Counters and histograms never appear, no errors anywhere | `temporality` is `cumulative` or unset; Dynatrace accepts the export with a 2xx and drops it |
| Exporter logs 404s | Endpoint uses the `.apps.` host instead of `.live.`, or a collector-style path like `/v1/metrics` instead of `/api/v2/otlp/v1/metrics` |
| Metric visible in DQL but "not found" in the classic Metrics API (or vice versa) | The classic Metrics API addresses OTLP metrics with an `ext:` prefix; DQL uses the plain dotted key |

## Follow best practices

- This dashboard is a starting point. Modify it to suit your particular needs.
- Be aware of metric cardinality. Every attribute multiplies series count, and Dynatrace bills on ingested data points. Keep high-cardinality attributes such as `graphql.operation.name` off metrics in production.
- In high-traffic environments, keep the trace sampler well below `1.0` to avoid Dynatrace rate limits.
